subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Taylor <aisha.taylor@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-15T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Hi Aisha — thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-up qualification questions so we can scope the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Recap from call:
- Primary use case: document ingestion + PII redaction and customer Q&A. Some workloads will handle highly sensitive customer PII.
- Current infra: FinSecure runs in AWS us-east-1 with strict VPC egress controls for sensitive workloads.
- Main concern: ensuring data used for inference never leaves FinSecure controlled environment OR is encrypted/ephemeral per your policy.

Key questions to confirm (short answers are fine):
1) Do you require that inference data and model inputs/outputs never leave your VPC (strict air-gap/on-prem requirement), OR would a Private VPC with peering and no public egress satisfy you?
2) For non-PII/lightly redacted pipelines, is using our Hosted API acceptable if we can ensure request-level redaction and no long-term storage?
3) Is customer-managed encryption (KMS/HSM) required for keys?
4) Do you need full request-level audit logs (and for how long)?
5) Rough QPS / concurrency and latency SLOs we should plan for?

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_Private_Summary.pdf (short matrix on differences + recommended initial architectures).

Next steps I recommend:
- If you need air-gapped/on-prem for any pipeline, we scope that separately — please indicate which pipelines require on-prem.
- Schedule a short architecture review with our Solutions Architect (Mateo) next week to validate network flows and KMS options.

If you can reply with the 1–5 answers above, I’ll loop in engineering and get a runbook + timeline together.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Taylor <aisha.taylor@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-16T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Thanks Marissa — quick answers below and a few follow-ups.

Answers to your numbered list:
1) For our PII-sensitive pipelines (customer records, KYC), data must not leave our VPC. That means on-prem or an air-gapped deployment for those flows.
2) For lower-risk pipelines (public knowledge base Q&A and general chatbots), Private VPC with strict peering and no public egress would be acceptable. Hosted API only for fully anonymized/redacted data.
3) Yes — customer-managed KMS is required for any data at rest.
4) We need detailed request-level audit logs retained for at least 1 year for the PII pipelines; shorter retention is OK for others.
5) Expected starting concurrency: ~30 qps for redaction pipeline peak, target 200 ms p95 latency. Fine-tuning workflows (future) may have lower qps but larger data transfer requirements.

Follow-ups:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood's KV cache or model serving caches can be disabled or set to zero retention for on-prem/private deployments? We cannot allow ephemeral caches that write to any external service.
- Do you have any documented guidance on network topology for Private VPC peering and firewall rules?

If you can confirm those items, we can lock down which pipelines need on-prem vs private VPC. Happy to schedule the architecture call — Tue/Wed next week works for us.

Best,
Aisha Taylor
Head of Product Security, FinSecure
aisha.taylor@finsecure.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Taylor <aisha.taylor@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-16T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Aisha — thanks, that’s really helpful. Quick answers inline and next steps.

On cache behavior:
- Our Dedicated offering runs tenant-isolated GPU pools and does not share KV caches across tenants; however, caching is enabled by default to optimize latency. For Private VPC or on-prem we can disable KV/prefix caching entirely or configure zero-retention policies. For on-prem (air-gap) there is no external caching — everything stays behind your network per the deployment.

On KMS / encryption:
- We support customer-managed KMS for both Dedicated and Private deployments; for on-prem deployments you can integrate your HSM/KMS (we provide connectors and config guidance).

On audit logs and logging controls:
- Request logs and full audit trails are configurable. For Private/Dedicated we can deliver logs to your S3 bucket or a self-hosted collector with retention policies you control. SOC2 evidence and examples attached.

Network topology + firewall guidance:
- See runbook: https://redwood.app/runbooks/private-deployment — it includes VPC peering patterns, allowed ports, and example security groups. For the architecture review we’ll walk through route tables and egress-blocking options.

Attachments: SOC2-snapshot.pdf (redacted report excerpt) + the summary I sent earlier.

Proposed next steps / times:
- Architecture review (30–45m) w/ Mateo (Solutions Architect) and our infra engineer. Proposed slots: Tue Jun 22 10:00–10:45 ET or Wed Jun 23 11:00–11:45 ET. Please confirm which works for you.

Rachel — can you pull the SOC2 evidence bundle and the integration checklist for the team so we can send ahead of the call?

Aisha — once you confirm the call I’ll set up a shared folder and a short mutual action plan so we can align timelines (RDW-2027-045).

Thanks,
Marissa
